detailed_sections.full_notes: Demography studies population size, composition, and trends. Core metrics include Birth Rate, Mortality Rate, Migration, and Total Fertility Rate. A fertility rate of 2.1 is replacement level fertility needed to maintain stable population size over generations.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Replacement Level Fertility
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A fertility rate of 2.1 children per woman, ensuring that children replace parents accounting for early mortality.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 6.2 Demographic Transition and India's Youth Bulge
detailed_sections.full_notes: Societies transition through 3 stages: Stage 1 (High birth & death rates), Stage 2 (Low death rate, high birth rate -> rapid growth), Stage 3 (Low birth & death rates -> stabilization/aging). India is in Stage 3, enjoying a massive working-age demographic dividend (15-64 years) that peaks before 2050.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Demographic Dividend
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Economic growth potential resulting from a shift in a population's age structure, where the working-age proportion (15–64) exceeds non-working dependents.
